en: Earth's seasons are caused by its 23.5-degree axial tilt, not by how far Earth is from the Sun.
Clouds are made of tiny liquid water droplets or ice crystals, not water vapor, which is an invisible gas.
The Sun generates energy through nuclear fusion in its core, not by burning fire like a campfire.
The Moon does not produce its own light; it shines by reflecting sunlight off its rocky surface.
Polaris, the North Star, is not the brightest star in the sky; Sirius is the brightest, while Polaris ranks only about 48th.
Venus is the hottest planet because its thick carbon dioxide atmosphere traps heat, even though Mercury is closer to the Sun.
Weather describes atmospheric conditions on a single day, while climate is the average weather pattern measured over at least 30 years.
Earthquakes occur when stress suddenly releases along a fault line, not from tectonic plates continuously grinding together.
Lightning can strike the same location many times; the Empire State Building gets struck by lightning about 25 times every year.
Soil has distinct horizontal layers called horizons, each with different amounts of rock fragments, organic matter, and minerals, rather than being one uniform layer.
A rock is a solid made of one or more minerals, while a mineral is a naturally formed solid with a specific chemical composition.
Groundwater does not flow in underground rivers; it slowly moves through tiny spaces and cracks between rocks and soil particles beneath the surface.
